...Nothing.
Next, I checked the remaining desks.
I searched every inch inside the desks, too.
...Nothing.
I searched every inch of the room, corner to corner.
It didn't seem to be in this classroom.{p}
Where should I go?
I decided to go to the classroom on the far right.{p}

Just then, a gust of wind blew in at me.
When I looked, I saw that a window was broken.{p}Should I go over and take a closer look?
Go over
Don't go
There was no need for that.{p}
Now, where should I go?

I spun around.
...But no one was there.
Was Hino watching me from somewhere?
Or was it the evil spirit said to lurk in this old school building?
Either way, it gave me a bad feeling.
I moved away from the window.{p}
Now, where should I go next?
I went to the sixth classroom from the left.{p}

I went into the classroom and shone my flashlight around.
Anything particularly out of the ordinary...
There it was.
A small pouch sat all alone on a desk, as if someone had left it behind.
My heart gave a jolt.
Could the ampoule be inside it?
The pouch was tied tightly shut with a cord.
With fingers slippery with sweat, I fumbled impatiently at the knot.
Then I shoved my hand inside.{p}

"Ow★"
A searing pain shot through my finger.
When I looked, there was a cut.
Blood was pouring out of it.
Someone had planted a razor blade inside the pouch.
What a vicious, underhanded trick.
It had to be Hino and the others.
Using my mouth and my free hand, I somehow managed to cover the wound with my handkerchief.
The throbbing pain pounded inside my head.
The cut seemed to be deeper than it looked.
In no time at all, the handkerchief was soaked red.
I felt like I was about to pass out.
Now I had to hurry even more than before.
If the bleeding didn't stop, my body would give out before the poison even had a chance to spread.{p}
I had to hurry.
I decided to go to the sixth classroom from the left.{p}

I searched every inch of the room, corner to corner.
It didn't seem to be in this classroom.{p}
Where should I go?
That was enough of the second-floor classrooms for now.

I decided to go to the second-floor restrooms.
There was a boys' restroom and a girls' restroom.{p}Which one should I search?
The boys' restroom
The girls' restroom
Search somewhere else
I decided to search the second-floor boys' restroom.{p}

I strangled Fukuzawa right back.
She might have caught me off guard, but she was still a girl.
If I really put my strength into it, I was bound to win.
Before long, Fukuzawa slumped limply to the floor.{p}

I'd tried to be careful not to kill her, though.
Anyway, I let out a breath.
I was saved.
Now all I had to do was drink this ampoule...{p}

The instant I let my guard down, a shadow sprang at me.
It was Fukuzawa, who should have been out cold.
"Kyeeeeeeeeh!"
She clawed my hand and knocked the ampoule flying.
The ampoule sailed out the window.
No!
I leaned out the window.
Glinting faintly, the ampoule fell toward the dark schoolyard.
Without that, I...!{p}

Just then, I was shoved from behind with tremendous force.
I lost my balance, and my body pitched out the window.
No way.
This is the third floor★{p}

I bent down to pick up the mechanical pencil.
Fukuzawa kicked straight up at my face, her shoe still on her foot.{p}

Along with the pale yellow liquid, blood ran down, one trickle, then two.
She licked it off with a flick of her tongue and laughed.
"Game over."
No...
This can't be happening.
After everything I went through, this is the end?
Am I just going to die now?
"Oh, I love that look on your face. Come on, show me more and more of how much it hurts to lose. Make that I-want-to-live face."
Fukuzawa said it gleefully.
Her eyes were sparkling.
She really seemed to be having the time of her life.
As I stared at her, a pitch-black rage swelled up inside me.{p}

I strangled her.
"Kya... st-sto..."
She was in agony.
That's it, suffer more.
Suffer my share, too.
Take the blame for my death.
"............ngh!"{p}
Her struggling hands flopped down.{p}

When I let go, she slumped to the floor.
Foam on her lips, Fukuzawa was dead.
This is fine.
Death won't be so lonely if I'm not dying alone.
I sat down next to Fukuzawa's corpse and hugged my knees.
Before dawn came, I would die.
Here in the old school building, maybe without anyone ever finding me.
But by now, even that was all right.
I had lost.{p}
I went tumbling over.{p}

A sharp, stabbing pain shot through my palm.
The shock of the fall had broken the ampoule.
Desperately, I licked up the yellow liquid running out with my blood.
Behind me, Fukuzawa laughed.
"Kyahahaha, no use, no use.
They say you have to drink the whole dose of that antidote, or it's pointless.
If you only drink a little, it actually makes the poison work faster."{p}

What?
As I tried to turn around, the strength drained softly out of my body.
My body went numb.
Is this the poison taking effect?
"It's working already? Lord Hino really is amaaazing."
Fukuzawa's delighted voice.
But by then, I couldn't even see her anymore.
After I'd come this far...
Without even time to grind my teeth, my consciousness sank into darkness.{p}
I shouted the title of the report at the top of my voice.{p}

But Fukuzawa didn't stop.
With her teeth still sunk into me, she pulled another mechanical pencil from her pocket.{p}

Then, in one swift motion, she drove it into my eye.
A shock like a red-hot poker rammed all the way into the center of my brain.
I couldn't even tell whether I was screaming or not.
In pain like my brains were being churned, I could only writhe helplessly.
The next instant, the finishing blow came down on me.{p}

Truthfully, I wanted to go home right away.
But my legs wouldn't move.
Exhaustion and relief made my whole body feel heavy.
I leaned against the wall.
I closed my eyes for a moment.
I'll rest, just a little.
Yes, just a little...
Thinking that, I ended up dozing off.{p}

...Something smelled like burning.
By the time I noticed and woke up, it was already too late.{p}

"Whoops, I'm not letting you through here."
It was Kazama!
He had his arms spread wide, blocking the hallway.
"What do you think you're doing? If you don't run, you'll die too★"
"I won't die. I'm immortal, after all."
...What is with this guy?
Is he seriously saying that?
But right now, I can't waste time on a guy like him.
I have to get out of here, fast.{p}What should I do?
Slip past Kazama
Run the opposite way from Kazama

I turned my back on Kazama and ran.
I had to get out of here before the fire spread!{p}

But...
The hallway ahead was a dead end.{p}

"Heh, too bad."
Kazama, who had chased after me, laughed.
"Now, prepare yourself."
...If it's come to this, it's all or nothing!
I threw myself at Kazama, shoulder first.{p}
But the instant we should have collided, Kazama vanished in a flash.{p}

Meeting nothing but air, I fell to the hallway floor.
The next instant, something burning hot was thrust into my neck.
Like a switch had been flipped off, the strength drained out of my body.
I can't stand...?
And then, what is this?
This stuff flowing out of my neck...{p}

Kazama was looking down at me as I lay there.
...Why does this guy look like he's having so much fun?
With him this wide open, I feel like I could still get away.
But my body won't obey me.
Worse, my hands and feet seem to be going cold.{p}

Oh, Kazama's leaving.
...Right, there's a fire, isn't there.
If I don't run, I'll burn to death.
With the little strength I had left, I desperately tried to get up.
At that moment, I thought I saw the Grim Reaper's scythe swinging down.{p}

I flew down the stairs.
Kazama reached the landing.
"{a}☆"
I whirled around with a start.{p}

...I will never forget that sight as long as I live.
Kazama, brandishing a gleaming kitchen knife as he ran down the stairs at me, lost his footing.
His face twisted in terror.
He was falling toward me.
And then.{p}

When I came to my senses, Kazama was lying right beside me.
The kitchen knife was buried deep in his chest.
What an anticlimactic way to die.
But strangely, it seemed to suit Kazama somehow.
Come on, there's no time to dawdle.{p}
I ran down the stairs and headed for the exit.{p}

Hino was there.
He was grinning.
"Not bad at all, {a}. I underestimated you. Why don't you join me? The Murder Club, I mean."
Hino smiled, his face perfectly pleasant.{p}

"............Don't be stupid. I'd sooner die."
"...I see. That's a shame. I thought you'd make a good partner.
I've disposed of every one of the traitors. Kazama, Shindo, Hosoda too. There's no one left.
And I'm graduating soon.
I thought you could take over after me and make a fine club president. Well?
Won't you reconsider?"{p}

"No way."
"So stubborn. Well, it can't be helped. Then I'll give up on you.
The Murder Club ends with me."
As we talked, I moved step by step toward Hino.
"Hino. There's one thing I want to ask you."
"What is it?"
"What is a Murder Club even for?"{p}

"I'm so glad you asked.
You see, people build up this thing called stress.
But the elite must never let stress build up. So what do you do about it?
That's right. You eliminate anything that might cause you stress.
You kill every last person who makes you angry.
That way, stress never builds up, and whatever stress you have just naturally melts away.
It's fun. Is there any other method as wonderful as this?"
"You're out of your mind."
"...Thank you. I'll take that as a compliment.
In every age, ordinary people never understand what a genius thinks.
Now, let's bring this to an end."{p}
